name: Question 9
problem:
A metal ball of mass $0.5\,\text{kg}$ is released from rest and falls vertically downward. Let $v(t)$ be the ball's velocity, in meters per second, $t\ge 0$ seconds after release, with downward taken as the positive direction.
The air resistance on the ball is proportional to the square of its velocity with a constant of proportionality $k=0.784\,\text{kg/m}$ and acts in the direction opposite to motion.

Find the equation for the velocity $v(t).$ Assume the acceleration due to gravity is $g=9.8\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ and the only forces acting on the ball are the weight due to gravity and drag.

Question 9

A metal ball of mass 0.5kg is released from rest and falls vertically downward. Let v(t) be the ball's velocity, in meters per second, t≥0 seconds after release, with downward taken as the positive direction. The air resistance on the ball is proportional to the square of its velocity with a constant of proportionality k=0.784kg/m and acts in the direction opposite to motion.

Find the equation for the velocity v(t). Assume the acceleration due to gravity is g=9.8m/s2, and the only forces acting on the ball are the weight due to gravity and drag.

a
 v(t)=52tanh⁡(2gt)
b
 v(t)=5tanh⁡(25gt)
c
 v(t)=52tanh⁡(gt)
d
 v(t)=2tanh⁡(25gt)
e
v(t)=52tanh⁡(25gt)
